result.response:
I have resolved the issue by updating `django.core.mail.utils.CachedDnsName` and `django.core.mail.message.make_msgid` to handle non-ASCII domain names and unicode hostnames properly:

1. In [`django/core/mail/utils.py`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-4am8nvnt/django/core/mail/utils.py#L10-L21), updated [`CachedDnsName.get_fqdn`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-4am8nvnt/django/core/mail/utils.py#L14-L18) to convert hostnames returned by `socket.getfqdn()` into IDNA ASCII (punycode).
2. In [`django/core/mail/message.py`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-4am8nvnt/django/core/mail/message.py#L114-L126), wrapped [`make_msgid`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-4am8nvnt/django/core/mail/message.py#L114-L126) so domain names passed in (or defaulting to `DNS_NAME`) are converted to IDNA ASCII before creating Message-IDs.
3. Added tests in [`tests/mail/tests.py`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-4am8nvnt/tests/mail/tests.py#L409-L425) to verify that non-ASCII domain names generate valid IDNA ASCII Message-IDs and pass header validation under non-unicode encodings (e.g. `iso-8859-1`).
